title: Profile
description: Current-user profile editor. Uses `core-data` `useEntityRecord('root','user', userId)`. Edits name fields, email, website, bio, interface language (`locale`), and a basic new-password change.

userId.description: User id to edit. The /users/{id}/edit route interpolates {id} here so the form targets the named user. Absent (e.g. the self-service /profile screen) → falls back to window.wpAdminWorkspaces.userId (the acting user).

documentation.purpose: Profile editor for the user named by `config.userId` (the acting user, `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.userId`, when `config.userId` is absent). Edits first/last/nickname, display name (chosen from a generated option set), email, website, biographical info, interface language (`locale`), and a basic new-password change under an 'Account Management' section. Reads + writes go through `core-data` `useEntityRecord('root', 'user', userId)`; the save button is disabled until `hasEdits` (or a new password is entered) and shows a loading state while `isSaving`. The new password is write-only (never returned by REST), held in local state and saved via a direct one-shot `saveEntityRecord('root','user',userId,{password})` call that NEVER enters the shared entity edits — a failed or abandoned password save cannot linger in the edits and be silently committed on a later unrelated save. Profile field edits go through the normal `save()` path (Step 1); the password goes through a separate `saveEntityRecord` call after the profile save succeeds (Step 2). The confirm-mismatch Notice clears as soon as the user retypes either the new password or confirm field. `useEntitySave` is called with entity coords (`{ kind:'root', name:'user', recordId:userId }`) so REST 4xx/5xx failures are caught via `getLastEntitySaveError` and surfaced as error banners rather than false-positive success snackbars. Success + error route through `@wordpress/notices` snackbar / banner. Below the form, an Application Passwords section (`ApplicationPasswords.js`) lists / creates (with one-time plaintext reveal) / revokes / revokes-all the user's application passwords via imperative `api-fetch` against `/wp/v2/users/{userId}/application-passwords`. Covers both the own-profile sub-screen of wp-admin's `users.php?action=editself` flow and (via `config.userId`) the `user-edit.php` edit surface the `core:users` Edit action routes to; the multi-user list lives in `core:users` (`docs/screens/users.md`).

reads.purpose: Profile fields of the edited user (config.userId, else the acting user).
Interface-language select options (Site Default + English + installed locales) built by PHP `wp_admin_workspaces_get_profile_languages()`. Falls back to a Site Default + English pair when absent.
User id to edit (interpolated from the /users/{id}/edit route); falls back to the acting user when absent.
Identify the acting user (fallback when config.userId is absent); absence of both shows a permission-denied message.
List the user's application passwords (Application Passwords section). Imperative api-fetch (not core-data) because the create response returns the plaintext `password` exactly once.

writes.purpose: Step 1: saves accumulated `edit()` calls via `save()` from useEntityRecord (all profile fields including `locale`). Step 2 (when a new password was entered): a separate one-shot `saveEntityRecord('root','user',{ id: userId, password })` call — the record object carries `id` so core-data issues a PATCH update, not a POST create. Failure is detected by the `undefined` return value + `getLastEntitySaveError('root','user',userId)` (saveEntityRecord does NOT throw on REST error); on failure an error notice is shown and password fields are left filled for retry. The password never enters the shared entity edits — failed or abandoned password saves cannot pollute a later profile save.
POST a new application password (name only); the response carries the plaintext `password` once for a one-time reveal.
Revoke a single application password by uuid (after a confirm modal).
Revoke all application passwords (after a confirm modal).

Same form with Save enabled; field edits report dirty-state to kernel (a pending password alone does not — it is local state until save).

Inline error Notice under the password fields; save is aborted until the two match. The Notice is cleared immediately when the user retypes either the new password or the confirm field (onChange on both fields).
Save button shows loading spinner + disabled state.

states.renders: Centered Spinner inside the Application Passwords section.
Create form + 'No application passwords have been created yet.'
Create form + a table (name / created / last used / last IP / Revoke) + Revoke-all button.

states.when: A new application password was just created

Notice.Root (intent=warning) with the server error message; the create form is hidden.

interactions.effect: `edit({ name: value })` with options generated from username / first / last / first+last / last+first / nickname / current name.
`edit({ locale: value })`; empty value ('') resets to Site Default. Only installed locales + English are offered (REST `locale` enum); installing a new pack on save is wp-admin-only and not surfaced.

interactions.trigger: Type a new password or confirm
interactions.effect: Held in local state. Retyping either field clears any pending mismatch Notice immediately. On Save: if the two differ, an inline error Notice shows and save aborts; if they match, the password is saved via a one-shot `saveEntityRecord` call (never enters shared edits). Password fields cleared on success.

Step 1: if `hasEdits`, calls `save()` via `handleSave` (profile fields); on failure returns early. Step 2: if a new password was entered, calls `saveEntityRecord('root','user',{ id: userId, password })` directly (record carries `id` so core-data issues PATCH, not POST); `saveEntityRecord` RESOLVES `undefined` on REST failure (does NOT throw) — detected via falsy return + `getLastEntitySaveError('root','user',userId)`; on failure shows error banner + leaves password fields filled for retry. On full success: snackbar ('Profile updated.' when profile edits were present; 'Password updated.' when only password changed) + password fields cleared.

interactions.trigger: Type a name + Add New Application Password (Application Passwords section)
interactions.effect: POST /wp/v2/users/{userId}/application-passwords { name }; reveals the returned plaintext password once, refreshes the list, success snackbar.
Opens a confirm Modal; on confirm DELETE the single uuid (or the collection), refreshes the list, success snackbar.

a11y.focus-management: Form fields are in document order; native focus order is sufficient.

constraints.note: `useEntityRecord('root','user', userId)` returns `{ record: null }` while loading. Reading `record.first_name` without a guard crashes on first paint.

Display name dropdown options are computed in render from the record's name fields. A field combination that produces only one option still renders the select; the user is forced to keep that option even if it's not what they want.

Manifest declares `core:dirty-state: true`. The app does NOT call `useDirtyState` directly — it relies on `hasEdits` being read by a sibling NavigationGuard. (`block-navigation-on-dirty` is intentionally not set; profile edits are low-stakes.)

The display-name select (`Edit: 'select'`) and the bio textarea (`Edit: { control: 'textarea', rows: 5 }`) are rendered by `DataForm` from their field definitions — they are DataViews-internal controls, NOT direct `@wordpress/components` imports. The app's only direct `@wordpress/components` leakage is `Spinner`.

The create response's plaintext `password` is shown exactly once and is never re-fetchable (`controller:625`). The reveal panel must stay imperative (`api-fetch`, local state) — a core-data entity cache would lose it. Dismissing or navigating away discards it permanently.

The new-password field has NO current-password re-authentication (REST does not require it) and NO server-side weak-password gate — `WP_REST_Users_Controller` accepts any password except those containing a backslash (`check_user_password`). The app only enforces a client-side confirm-match. The classic wp-admin pass1/pass2 + zxcvbn strength meter + `pw_weak` confirm checkbox are intentionally not reproduced. `password` is never returned by REST, so it lives in local state (not the entity record edits) and is saved via a direct one-shot `saveEntityRecord` call at save time — it never enters the shared edit queue.

Interface Language offers only Site Default + English + already-installed locales (the REST `locale` enum is `en_US` + `get_available_languages()` plus '' for site default). Installing a downloadable language pack on save is a wp-admin-only sub-feature and is deliberately not offered. REST resolves `locale` via `get_user_locale()`, so a site-default user reads back the resolved site locale (not '') — selecting Site Default ('') writes the reset.

Application passwords require HTTPS and are incompatible with Basic-Auth-protected sites; the controller gates server-side. A failed list GET renders an inline unavailable notice (and hides the create form) rather than crashing the profile form.

The section manages `userId`'s passwords (the acting user on the self-service /profile screen). Managing another user's application passwords requires the `edit_user` cap; the REST controller enforces this, so an under-privileged admin editing another user sees the unavailable notice.

design-system-leakage.purpose: Profile form layout + password inputs + password-mismatch Notice + save button. URL + email fields are DataForm field defs (type: 'text'/'email') — DataViews owns their rendering; `InputControl` is used only for the write-only new-password / confirm-password fields.
Loading spinner — no `@wordpress/ui` 0.12 port. The display-name select and bio textarea are `DataForm` `Edit` controls (DataViews-internal), not direct DS imports.
Application Passwords section — create form, list heading, unavailable warning notice, never-used pill.
Application Passwords — revoke-confirm modal, destructive Revoke buttons (no WPDS 0.12 critical tone), section divider, list spinner.
